meeting_window.summary: 本次會議深入探討了 agent 的記憶系統架構，特別是短期與長期記憶之間的關係與更新機制。團隊回顧了現有的 L1-L3 三層階層式記憶結構，並討論了從逐字稿生成 L1 idea units 的過程。會議中提出了兩項重要的新方法：(1) 在 agent 的「使用階段」，利用 LLM 的 function-calling 功能，讓模型動態決定要查詢短期或長期記憶；(2) 在「更新階段」也採用類似方法，透過逐句分析，決定資訊應更新至哪個記憶庫。此外，會議也強調了為了提升 LLM 分析的準確性，需要對逐字稿進行預處理，將其切分為更小的 idea units。然而，關於記憶整合的具體標準、不同記憶類型間的確切關係等架構性問題仍待解決。
key_points: 團隊闡明了 L1 (單次會議筆記)、L2 (多次會議摘要) 與 L3 (最高層級摘要) 的三層式記憶架構。 (證據: L13-19)
一項核心架構提議是讓短期和長期記憶從原始逐字稿中獨立更新，而非讓資訊從短期依序流向長期記憶。 (證據: L91-94, L107)
針對 agent 的「使用階段」，提出讓 LLM 透過 function-calling 根據使用者問題，動態決定查詢短期或長期記憶，取代固定的系統邏輯。 (證據: L47-59, L66-79)
延伸 function-calling 的概念，建議在「更新階段」也導入此機制，透過逐句分析逐字稿，讓 LLM 決定該資訊要更新到短期還是長期記憶。 (證據: L109-113)
會議確定在將逐字稿交給 LLM 分析前，需先進行預處理，將其切分為「idea units」，以提高資訊抽取的準確度。 (證據: L39-45)
系統設計包含一個追蹤「重新出現主題」的機制，該機制使用基於「新近度 (Recency)」和「重要性 (Importance)」的評分系統，並設有衰減下限，以防主題被完全遺忘。 (證據: L22-25)
目前預設的 L1 物件類型 (如：決策、待辦事項、開放問題) 被視為一個有效的初步假設，同時也是系統當前的限制之一。 (證據: L31-38)
open_questions: 記憶鞏固機制：資訊被整合到長期記憶的具體標準是什麼（例如：頻率、重要性、時間衰減）？短期和長期記憶之間的更新流程與關係尚未最終確定。 (證據: L81-90, L107)
檢索分數權重：結合了語意相似度、新近度和重要性的檢索分數，其權重應如何計算與評估？ (證據: L26)
初始 Idea Unit 生成：從原始逐字稿中叢集並生成 L1「idea units」的最佳方法或 prompt 是什麼？ (證據: L27-30)
系統邏輯 vs. LLM 邏輯：團隊對於使用寫死的系統邏輯，或是讓 LLM 決定查詢哪個記憶庫的優劣進行了辯論，最佳方法仍在討論中。 (證據: L66-79)
定義記憶特徵：在此 agent 的架構中，短期和長期記憶在結構和內容上的明確差異是什麼（例如：節點數量、內容密度）？ (證據: L80)

meeting_window.summary: 本次會議深入探討了記憶更新的架構。團隊比較了兩種處理逐字稿的方法：一種是使用LLM工具調用（Tool Calling）進行迭代和動態分塊，另一種是預處理步驟以預先分組「想法單元」（idea units）。會議詳細介紹了短期記憶（包含行動項目和近期會議摘要）和長期記憶（用於上下文摘要的L1-L3層次結構）的結構。支持這種分離的一個關鍵理由是長期記憶中的「遺忘」機制，該機制利用衰減的相關性和重要性分數來提高即時檢索效率。團隊還規劃了評估策略，包括將其系統與標準RAG進行比較，並利用團隊自身的會議歷史來展示長期記憶和「遺忘」功能，以準備即將在五月舉行的專題展覽。
key_points: 討論了使用LLM工具調用進行動態、迭代式處理逐字稿以形成「想法單元」的方法，並與靜態分塊或預分組方法進行了比較。
闡明了記憶架構：短期記憶保存行動項目和近期會議摘要，而長期記憶則採用層次化（L1-L3）結構，用於跨時間的上下文摘要。
提出了「遺忘」機制作為劃分長短期記憶的關鍵理由，該機制基於衰減的相關性和重要性分數，旨在提高即時檢索的效率。
確認了五月專題展的計畫，重點展示長期記憶能力和「想法單元」的打包過程。
提出了一項評估策略：利用團隊自身的會議歷史，將系統與標準RAG模型進行比較，以突顯「遺忘」機制的優勢。
open_questions: 將對話分割為「想法單元」的最佳方法是什麼？是所提出的動態迭代方法、使用LLM進行預分組，還是其他方法？
如何利用團隊自身的會議歷史作為數據集，有效地展示「遺忘」機制？
目前的五次會議數據是否足以展示長期記憶的效果，或者是否需要一個更大、可能需要人工生成的數據集？

meeting_window.summary: 本次會議聚焦於兩大主軸：定義評估計畫，以及針對記憶更新流程的深度架構辯論。團隊規劃了多面向的評估策略，包含短期正確性、長期演進追蹤、決策推理，以及一項創新的「遺忘 (fade-out)」指標。大量的討論集中在系統架構，權衡了由LLM驅動的函式調用方法與更具程式化控制的逐步流程之間的優劣。此番討論催生了「管理者-代理人 (Manager-Agent)」架構的提案，旨在透過一個管理者將任務指派給專門的代理人，以提升系統的可控性與可觀察性。團隊同時也討論了資料量的充足性、腦力激盪了資料增強的策略，並透過分配預算解決了API的計費問題。
key_points: 定義評估計畫：評估將涵蓋三個主要類別：短期正確性、長期演進追蹤和決策推理。(L18-22, L108-111)
提出創新的「遺忘 (Fade-Out)」指標：提出一項新指標，用於評估系統在不永久刪除資訊的情況下，遺忘不重要資訊的能力，此方法與標準的RAG刪除作法形成對比。(L23-28, L112-122)
規劃消融研究 (Ablation Study)：計畫進行一項消融研究，將完整系統與基線（僅RAG、僅短期、僅長期）進行比較，以證明其組合式架構的優越性。(L42-49, L123-127)
討論資料稀缺性與增強策略：認為當前資料集（5次會議，180分鐘）可能不足，並討論了資料增強策略，例如使用AI擴展對話或整合其他專案的資料。(L4-17, L99-107)
核心架構辯論：會議的中心議題是當前「由上而下」的固定視窗處理方式，與提案的「由下而上」的動態「想法單元 (idea unit)」切分方法之間的衝突。(L70-92, L128-160)
提出「管理者-代理人」架構：為解決當前LLM驅動工作流程在可控性與可靠性上的問題，提出了一個「管理者-代理人」架構。由一個中心管理者透過指派任務（如逐字稿切分、記憶更新）給專門的代理人來協調流程。(L282-320)
解決API計費問題：為了解決Gemini API點數未能正確應用的問題，團隊決定撥款20,000台幣預算給一位團隊成員處理。(L170-184)
open_questions: 在當前最先進的LLM-agent情境下，「長脈絡 (long context)」的精確定義與token數量為何？(L7-10, L102-104)
提案的「管理者-代理人」架構將如何實作？哪些特定的代理人會被優先創建？(L313-320)
在比較不同逐字稿切分方法（固定、動態、逐輪）的實驗中，將如何衡量計算成本、精確率和召回率之間的權衡？(L82-92, L161-169)
團隊是否會從其他學生的會議中獲取額外資料來擴充現有資料集？(L13-16, L105-107)

action_items.title: Define a method to prove the value of the memory architecture
action_items.detail: Following the discussion on memory architecture, a next step was proposed to define a method to prove the value of having the proposed long-term memory architecture.

action_items.title: Define the relationship and update mechanism for memory architectures
action_items.detail: Clarify the relationship between short-term and long-term memory and define how they are updated, including how information transitions between them.

action_items.title: Implement pre-processing for meeting transcriptions
action_items.detail: Implement a pre-processing step for meeting transcriptions, such as splitting them into sentences, before feeding them into the memory update system to improve accuracy and enable more fine-grained control.

action_items.title: Research the definition of 'long context' for LLMs
action_items.detail: To properly assess the sufficiency of the current 180-minute dataset, the team needs to research how 'long context' is defined for LLMs, specifically in terms of tokens, not minutes. This will provide a standard for comparison.

action_items.title: Acquire more meeting recording data from other students
action_items.detail: To augment the dataset, acquire past meeting recordings from other students. Specifically, contact senior student Zhen Ying (真盈) who also works on meeting analysis and is likely to have relevant data.

action_items.title: Conduct a literature review on LLM 'forgetting' mechanisms
action_items.detail: Review and list existing literature on how 'forgetting' is implemented in LLMs, distinguishing between RAG-based (external data removal) and fundamental model alteration approaches. A specific paper mentioned as 'Time Memory' should be located and included.

action_items.title: Test and evaluate the dynamic transcript processing method
action_items.detail: An agreement was made to test a new, more efficient dynamic method for processing meeting transcripts against an iterative or fixed-window summary approach. The evaluation should focus on metrics like compute cost, precision, and recall.

method_changes.before: The memory system uses absolute meeting IDs (e.g., '16', '17') to reference when an item was discussed.
method_changes.after: Proposed change to use relative time references (e.g., 'one week ago') for memory items.
method_changes.reason: A suggestion was made to make the timeline of memory items more intuitive and human-readable, changing from absolute meeting IDs to relative time.

method_changes.topic: Code development and data structure alignment
method_changes.after: The team decided to collaborate by modifying a shared open-source GitHub repository and align on a common folder structure.
method_changes.reason: To align development efforts and prevent data duplication, such as having multiple versions of meeting transcripts.

method_changes.before: Adopt an object-based structure for long-term memory, extracting specific object types.
method_changes.after: The long-term memory object structure is defined to include: 'Type' (e.g., decision, method), 'Content' (an LLM-generated summary), 'Evidence' (the original verbatim transcript lines), and 'Related Topics' (keywords for retrieval).
method_changes.reason: To establish a concrete schema for LTM objects that captures the summarized idea, its direct source from the transcript, and metadata to facilitate future retrieval.

method_changes.topic: Transcript Processing for Idea Unit Segmentation
method_changes.before: A pre-processing step is added to segment the transcript into smaller idea units (e.g., by sentence or turn) before feeding them to the LLM.
method_changes.after: Adopt an iterative, model-driven approach for transcript segmentation. Instead of fixed pre-processing, the model uses a 'Read' tool to dynamically decide how many lines of the transcript to process at once, allowing it to form cohesive 'idea units' without being constrained by predefined chunks. It can read a few lines, form a candidate idea, and then read more to merge and complete the idea.
method_changes.reason: This dynamic approach avoids the key limitation of fixed-chunking, which often splits a single idea across multiple chunks. It allows the model to handle overlapping ideas and form more accurate, contextually complete units for memory updates.

method_changes.topic: Relationship Between Short-Term and Long-Term Memory Updates
method_changes.before: An LLM will use function-calling to dynamically decide whether to update short-term memory, long-term memory, or both from a single stream.
method_changes.after: Short-term and long-term memory are updated in separate, independent processes. Each process receives the complete transcript and operates on its respective memory store without interaction during the update phase.
method_changes.reason: This approach was deemed more sensible as it simplifies the update pipeline and allows for specialized logic for each memory type, rather than having a single process decide the destination for each idea unit.

method_changes.after: Using WhisperX turn-based transcripts, which are manually corrected for speaker turns, as the standard input for the memory update process. This format is treated like a database where rows can be read programmatically.
method_changes.reason: To establish a standardized, structured input format that enables the model to programmatically read and process the conversation line-by-line or in dynamic chunks.

method_changes.after: The memory update process is structured into two distinct, model-controlled steps: 1) A 'Read' function is used to access the source transcript and the current state of the memory database. 2) A 'Write' function is used to modify the memory database with new or updated information.
method_changes.reason: To create a clear, programmatic flow for memory modification that is controlled by the LLM, separating the information gathering phase from the writing phase.

method_changes.topic: Proposed Advanced Segmentation Method: Information Entropy
method_changes.before: Dynamic segmentation is guided implicitly by the LLM.
method_changes.after: A specific method is proposed to make dynamic segmentation more efficient: use a metric like information entropy to predict the number of subsequent sentences that belong to the current topic. The model would dynamically adjust the 'chunk size' based on whether the topic diversity increases, allowing it to quickly find the optimal cut-point for an idea unit.
method_changes.reason: This is a potential improvement over simple iterative reading, aiming to balance computational cost with accuracy by intelligently 'jumping' forward a predicted number of sentences instead of processing one by one or in small, fixed steps.

method_changes.after: A two-pronged evaluation strategy is proposed: 1) Benchmark the dynamic idea unit creation method against baseline methods (fixed-size and sentence-by-sentence chunking). 2) Compare the performance of the dual short-term/long-term memory architecture against a standard RAG system.
method_changes.reason: To quantitatively and qualitatively demonstrate the value and novelty of the project's core technical contributions.

method_changes.before: Long-term memory is a flat collection of memory objects.
method_changes.after: Long-term memory is organized into a three-level hierarchy: L1 (the most low-level, individual memory objects generated from meetings), which are summarized into L2 (e.g., monthly summaries), and further into L3 (high-level, overall project context). This structure allows retrieval of an L1 item to also pull its broader L2/L3 context.
method_changes.reason: To provide contextual summarization at different levels of abstraction, enabling the agent to understand not just a specific fact, but also its broader temporal and thematic context.

method_changes.after: The team's own meeting history will be used as the primary dataset for evaluating the memory system.
method_changes.reason: This dataset is highly relevant and contains real examples of evolving topics, method changes, and forgotten ideas, making it ideal for demonstrating the system's long-term tracking and 'forgetting' capabilities.

method_changes.topic: Long-Term Memory Dynamics: Relevance and Forgetting
method_changes.before: Retrieval mechanism was not fully specified.
method_changes.after: LTM incorporates a 'forgetting' mechanism based on relevance and importance scores. A memory's relevance can decay over time if not referenced. However, it can be 're-awakened' if the topic is discussed again. A critical rule is that memories with an 'importance' score above a certain threshold will never fade out, ensuring essential information is preserved.
method_changes.reason: To model human-like memory, improving real-time retrieval efficiency by focusing on currently relevant topics while still retaining the ability to recall old information. The 'importance' score prevents the loss of critical, foundational knowledge.

method_changes.before: Using only the 5 meetings from the current project (180 minutes).
method_changes.after: Augmenting the dataset by 1) using an LLM to extend existing dialogues and 2) incorporating meeting recordings from other students/projects to increase data volume and contextual diversity.
method_changes.reason: The current dataset of 5 meetings may be insufficient for robust LLM training and evaluation.

method_changes.before: Evaluation questions were not formally categorized.
method_changes.after: Establishing a structured evaluation framework with three distinct categories: 1) Short-term correctness, 2) Long-term evolution tracking, and 3) Decision reasoning.
method_changes.reason: To systematically assess different capabilities of the memory system.

method_changes.before: Evaluation did not include a metric for the agent's ability to forget or ignore irrelevant information.
method_changes.after: Introducing a new evaluation metric to test the "fade out" of unimportant information. The agent should not surface these memories in general dialogue but they should remain in an "inactive" state, retrievable via specific queries or repeated mentions. This would be controlled by an importance weight.
method_changes.reason: To develop a more sophisticated and human-like memory system that avoids cluttering conversations with irrelevant long-term memories.

method_changes.before: No formal ablation study was defined.
method_changes.after: A formal ablation study is planned to prove the value of the full architecture. It will compare four conditions: 1) RAG-only baseline, 2) Short-term memory only, 3) Long-term memory only, and 4) The full system combining short and long-term memory.
method_changes.reason: To experimentally justify the complexity and components of the proposed memory architecture.

method_changes.before: Using a fixed-window approach (e.g., reading 20-40 lines at a time) and letting a single LLM call identify idea units within that chunk (a "top-down" approach).
method_changes.after: Agreed to test a new dynamic, "bottom-up" segmentation method. This involves the agent predicting the appropriate length of the next chunk based on the current sentence, aiming to create more semantically coherent blocks. The evaluation will compare this to fixed-window and turn-by-turn methods on metrics like compute cost, precision, and recall.
method_changes.reason: The fixed-window approach is arbitrary and may split or incorrectly group ideas, while a turn-by-turn approach is computationally expensive. The dynamic approach aims for a better trade-off between computational efficiency and segmentation accuracy.

method_changes.before: A monolithic approach where a single large prompt dictates the entire workflow, relying on LLM function calling to control the sequence of operations. This was found to be hard to control and debug.
method_changes.after: Proposal to switch to a "Manager-Agent" architecture. A programmatic "Manager" controls the high-level workflow, delegating specific, granular tasks to specialized "Agents" (e.g., an agent for splitting text into idea units, an agent for updating memory). The LLM is used within agents to perform tasks, not to control the overall flow.
method_changes.reason: To improve the system's reliability, controllability, debuggability, and modularity by replacing a single, complex LLM-driven control flow with a structured, programmatic one that orchestrates calls to specialized LLM-powered agents.

experiment_todos.description: Design and run an experiment to demonstrate the memory system's effectiveness, for example, by visualizing how an event's history is tracked by the agent compared to a baseline agent, or by designing questions that show different answers.
Research and review how related papers evaluate and prove their memory model's performance, including looking for standardized tests or benchmarking datasets.
Start implementing the new memory architecture by pulling and modifying the open-source GitHub repository.
Investigate prior work that uses the ICSI dataset, especially for memory-related tasks published after 2022.
Explore a two-step approach to model meeting 'style', specifically for handling interruptions, by first generating content and then applying a style model or flag.

Refine the evaluation for 'dead topics' to test the 'fade out' mechanism. The test should verify that unimportant/inactive topics do not appear in regular dialogue but can be retrieved from long-term memory via specific probes.
Implement a pre-processing step to segment transcripts into smaller idea units before analysis to improve LLM performance and reduce hallucination.
Experiment with using function calling to allow the agent to dynamically decide which memory (short-term or long-term) to access or update based on sentence-level analysis.
Compare the proposed dynamic idea unit creation method against fixed-size and sentence-by-sentence methods to evaluate its effectiveness and trade-offs.
Conduct an ablation study to justify the system's architecture by comparing the full system (short-term + long-term memory) against multiple baselines: RAG-only, short-term-only, and long-term-only.

Prepare a dataset for evaluation, potentially by generating dialogue sessions from existing meeting transcripts, to demonstrate long-term memory effects. Evaluate if the current 5 meetings are sufficient or if more data is needed.

Design and run a specific experiment to demonstrate long-term memory: query about a topic from a much older meeting (e.g., 20 meetings ago) and compare the model's response with a standard RAG model's response.
Experiment with using an LLM to augment the dataset by extending the dialogue in existing transcripts.
Acquire meeting recordings from senior student (真盈) to use as additional training/evaluation data for experiments.

next_meeting_focus: Finalize the agent-based architecture, focusing on the 'Manager-Agent' model and the implementation of dynamic, topic-aware transcript segmentation.
Establish a clear definition of 'long context' in terms of tokens and formulate a data strategy, including whether to augment existing data or acquire new meeting logs.
